name: tick_direction_momentum_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Consecutive upticks (price increases tick-to-tick) aggregated over 1-min bars reveal net buying pressure that predicts short-term continuation. In Indian markets, retail order flow is highly auto-correlated: when buying momentum starts, retail participants pile in with market orders creating a 2-5 minute momentum wave. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders watch price alone, not the underlying tick direction ratio. The edge is not arbitraged away because: (1) it requires tick-level data reconstruction, (2) the signal is noisy per-tick but aggregates well over 1-min bars, (3) the hold time is too short for most systematic funds but too data-intensive for manual retail traders.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

filters.expiry_filter: skip on F&O expiry days (theta burn distorts tick patterns)

weaknesses: Tick direction is a noisy proxy for order flow — a single large sell order hitting the bid doesn't register as many downticks but represents significant selling pressure.
Very tight stop (8 bps) means high probability of stop-outs in volatile stocks. The strategy may generate many small losses that erode the edge from winners.
Requires tick-level data feed that Zerodha's standard API doesn't provide at sufficient granularity; WebSocket feed has ~500ms latency.
prior_art: Blume, Easley & O'Hara (1994) 'Market Statistics and Technical Analysis'. Chordia, Roll & Subrahmanyam (2002) 'Order Imbalance, Liquidity, and Market Returns'. In India, Jain & Biswal (2016) study microstructure of NSE.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
